text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Insurer Aegon pays Dfl 6.1 billion for insurance activities of U.S. Providian Corporation. (p1)
- Prime minister Wim Kok by far the most popular Dutch politician according to a poll. (p1)
- Builder HBG buys 74 pct stake in German contractor Wayss & Freytag. (p1)
- The Midcap-index of 25 medium-sized companies outperforms the AEX-index on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange this year. (p1)
- Port and trading company HIM Furness calls off share issue. (p3)
- Philips Electronics' German subsidiary Grundig to shed another 2,000 jobs. (p3)
- Amsterdam given green light for the construction of a new port basin. (p6)
- Temp services group Goudsmit outperformer on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange this year, due to clear strategy. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Joint Amsterdam bourse-listed companies increase their quoted market value by 200 billion guilders this year. (p1)
- Financial services group Achmea takes 5.15 pct stake in insurer Stad Rotterdam. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Traditional New Year's Eve state lottery, first prize Dfl 10 million, sold out. (p1)
- Junior finance minister works on draft bill to solve problems with succession in small businesses. (p7)
- 55 pct of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker's employees have found another job. (p37)
- Tonight will the coldest New Year's eve for 20 years. (p1)
